issuing_body: Ministry of Science and ICT (과학기술정보통신부) / National Information Society Agency (NIA)
covered_actors: High-impact AI development business operators (인공지능개발사업자) developing and providing high-impact AI or integrating general-purpose AI models into high-impact AI systems

High-impact AI-using business operators (인공지능이용사업자) providing products or services utilizing high-impact AI (with partial exemption from Art. 34(1)(1)-(3) where no substantial functional modification occurs)

Overseas AI business operators without a domestic address/office exceeding Presidential Decree revenue or user thresholds (e.g., KRW 1 trillion revenue) and their designated domestic representatives (국내대리인)
Business operators adopting or fine-tuning open-source AI models for high-impact AI products or services
State agencies and public institutions deploying high-impact AI for public-service decision-making

enforcement_authorities: Ministry of Science and ICT (과학기술정보통신부 / MSIT)
National AI Committee (위원회, referenced under AI Basic Act Art. 34(1)(6) for deliberating additional high-impact AI safety/trustworthiness measures)
National Information Society Agency (한국지능정보사회진흥원 / NIA, referenced for High-Impact AI Determination Guideline support)
compliance_deadlines: 2026-01: Scheduled entry into force of the AI Basic Act (enacted 2024-12-26)

5-year retention period: Mandatory retention (written or electronic) of Safety and Trustworthiness Documents (안전신뢰문서) and compliance evidence under AI Basic Act Art. 34(1)(5) and Enforcement Decree Art. 27(2)
implementation_notes: 111-page official MSIT/NIA implementation guideline (2026-01-22) operationalizing High-Impact AI operator obligations under AI Basic Act Article 34, Enforcement Decree Article 27, and MSIT's Technical Notice across 10 statutory high-impact domains (energy, drinking water, healthcare/medical devices, nuclear facilities, law-enforcement biometrics, recruitment/loans, transportation, public-service decisions, and K-12 student assessment) plus GPAI models integrated into high-impact systems. Synthesizes TTA Trustworthy AI Development Guide, NIST AI RMF, and EU AI Act across five statutory duties—(1) lifecycle risk management & governance, (2) explainability & training-data overview disclosure, (3) user protection (data governance, adversarial robustness, testing, monitoring, feedback, redress/compensation), (4) human oversight (intervention triggers, emergency stop, inspections, training), and (5) 5-year Safety & Trustworthiness Document retention—with dedicated open-source model guidance in every chapter, trade-secret carve-outs, equivalence-statement flexibility, a blank document template, a 69-item TTA crosswalk, and a complete AI recruitment example.
